records.summary: 401 Columbus Ave sits in the North Beach NCD where a restaurant serving full liquor is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval (Planning Code §722 and §780.3). The space has a long history as a restaurant with multiple CUAs dating back to 1988, most recently approved for a Type 41 license in 2022 for Cassava restaurant. The block is extremely dense with 75 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 46 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 109 licenses within 1,000 ft—ABC's undue concentration flag is raised. The base rate shows only 6 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft over 5 years (1 approved, 4 approved with conditions, 1 withdrawn), too few to calculate an approval rate but suggesting conditional approvals are typical for alcohol intensifications here.

patterns.pattern: Type 47 upgrades at established restaurants in North Beach NCD require a Conditional Use Authorization hearing when they constitute a new intensification (Type 41→47, or new license after operations pause). When a restaurant in North Beach holds a prior Type 47 authorization and continues operations without a change of business, vacancy >18 months, or physical expansion, Planning treats a license transfer or renewal as 'continuation of existing use' and approves it by ABC/DPH referral without a new CUA.

CUA approvals for Type 47 in North Beach impose standard conditions: 3-year validity from decision, signage compliance (Article 6), odor control equipment and ducting not on primary facade, sidewalk maintenance per DPW standards, community liaison officer appointed before permit issuance, and garbage/compost/recycling storage. No hours restrictions or occupancy caps were imposed in the 2022 compa…

Multiple addresses on the same Columbus Ave and adjacent Green/Vallejo blocks (within 11–110 m of subject site) hold active alcohol authorizations (Type 41 and Type 47), indicating the Commission and Planning have found alcohol service in restaurants compatible with this immediate North Beach corridor despite high license density.

401 Columbus Ave has a multi-decade history of Commission-approved restaurant uses: 1988 CUA for small restaurant, followed by approvals in 1997, 2004 (Type 47 upgrade noted in record summary), and 2007 (expansion). North Beach SUD Planning Code Section 780.3(c)(1)(B) allows a restaurant to occupy a space last used as a restaurant without additional CUA process for the base use, but Section 780.3(c)(2)(A) subjects a restaurant serving full liquor to conditional use authorization. Recent referrals distinguish 'continuation of existing use and license type' (no CUA needed) from intensifications (CUA required).

findings.text: The address sits in the North Beach NCD and Special Use District, where a restaurant serving on-sale liquor (ABC Types 47, 41, etc.) is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval and a finding that it operates as a bona fide eating place (Planning Code §722 and §780.3(c)(2)(A)).

Five Conditional Use Authorizations are on file at 401 Columbus Ave: 1988 (small restaurant), 1997 (full-service restaurant), 2004 (beer/wine to Type 47 upgrade), 2007 (expansion to 2,040 sq ft), and 2009 (specialty food self-service use), the most recent decided March 2010.

In May 2022 Planning approved an ABC referral for a Type 41 (beer/wine) license at this address for Cassava restaurant, stating per §780.3(c)(1)(B) that a restaurant may occupy a space last used as a restaurant, and noting that the prior occupant Trattoria Pinocchio was also a full-service restaurant.

At 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away, same block and zoning), the Planning Commission in December 2022 approved a CUA to transfer a Type 47 license to Mona Lisa Mare e Monti restaurant, an existing restaurant upgrading from Type 41, taking 270 days from filing to approval.

A conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code §178), and upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 at this address constitutes an intensification of the alcohol service, not a continuation.

The description does not state whether the business is formula retail or whether the proposal changes any condition of the prior CUAs on file, so the rules could not decide whether formula retail prohibition or a condition-amendment trigger applies.

approvals.summary: The Type 47 license transfer requires ABC investigation, public posting, and Planning CUA approval, and the census tract is over its authorized on-sale license count, so a public convenience or necessity finding will likely be required.

findings.text: Census tract 107.02 has 22 active on-sale retail licenses against 5 authorized under ABC's September 2026 tract authorizations, triggering the undue concentration test under Business & Professions Code §23958.4.

When a census tract is over its authorized count, ABC may still issue or transfer a license if it finds that public convenience or necessity would be served, requiring the applicant to submit evidence and the city to provide a recommendation.
ABC refers all original applications and license transfers to SFPD (ABC Liaison Unit) and SF Planning Department for review; Planning's review will await or run concurrently with the CUA hearing.

Type 47 licenses are quota licenses limited to one per 2,000 county inhabitants; new ones are acquired by purchasing and transferring an existing license, which in San Francisco costs roughly $100,000–$450,000 plus 90–180 days for escrow, posting, and local sign-off.

The description states the applicant will obtain the Type 47 by premises-to-premises transfer, so the license acquisition and transfer timeline (including broker engagement, escrow, and ABC posting) runs in parallel with or before the CUA process.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is required and is issued after plan check and final inspection without a discretionary hearing, so it is allowed as of right once the restaurant's plans and operations are approved.

findings.text: Every food facility needs a health permit to operate, issued by SF Department of Public Health after plan check and pre-opening inspection confirm the facility matches approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff (California Retail Food Code §§114380–114381).
DPH permits are routed to Planning for zoning review; the May 2022 DPH referral at this address was approved as continuation of existing restaurant use.

Under the California Building Code a restaurant or bar is Assembly Group A-2, but a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B; the description does not give the occupant load, so the proposed occupancy group cannot be established.

The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records and can only be determined by plans or an inspection, so a Building Code change of occupancy cannot be established and the building permit requirements are not decided.

expected_conditions.condition: The restaurant must operate and maintain the licensed premises as a bona fide eating place, with food service as the primary use and alcohol incidental to meals.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code §780.3(c)(2)(A) requires a Commission finding that a restaurant serving liquor in the North Beach SUD is and will remain a bona fide eating place. The 2022 CUA at 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away) for a Type 47 upgrade included no specific food-percentage condition, reflecting the January 2024 amendment that removed the 51% receipts test, but the Commission's finding and ABC's Type 47 definition still require a bona fide eating place.

expected_conditions.condition: The restaurant must provide records of its gross receipts or gross sales to the Planning Department on request.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code §780.3(c)(2)(A) as amended January 14, 2024 (Ord. 249-23) replaced the 51% food-receipts test with a requirement that the restaurant give the Department gross receipts or sales records on request, applying to all North Beach restaurants with on-sale liquor licenses.

expected_conditions.condition: Odor control equipment is required, with ducting that does not run across the primary façade of the building.
expected_conditions.basis: The December 2022 CUA at 414 Columbus Ave for a Type 47 upgrade (43 m away, same block and zoning) imposed a standard condition requiring odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the building permit plans, with ducting not applied to the primary façade. This is a standard condition for eating and drinking uses in San Francisco.

expected_conditions.condition: The project sponsor must maintain the main entrance and all sidewalks abutting the property in a clean and sanitary condition per DPW standards.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code §202.2 imposes sidewalk maintenance conditions on all eating and drinking uses, and the December 2022 Type 47 CUA at 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away) included this as a standard condition. Every recent restaurant approval in the record set includes this requirement.

expected_conditions.condition: The project sponsor must appoint a community liaison officer and provide written notice of the liaison's name, address and telephone number to the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups before any permit is issued.
expected_conditions.basis: The December 2022 CUA at 414 Columbus Ave for a Type 47 upgrade imposed a community liaison condition, and it is a standard condition for conditional use authorizations of eating and drinking uses in North Beach and other neighborhood commercial districts.

expected_conditions.condition: The authorization is valid for three years from the effective date of the Motion; DBI must issue a building or site permit within that period or the sponsor must seek renewal or amendment.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard validity condition in every CUA, including the December 2022 approval at 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away). If no construction or change of use permit is pulled within three years the authorization lapses unless renewed.

expected_conditions.condition: All exterior signage must comply with Planning Code Article 6 and be designed to complement, not compete with, the existing architectural character of the building.
expected_conditions.basis: Signage condition imposed on the December 2022 Type 47 CUA at 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away, same historic North Beach corridor). Article 6 limits sign area, illumination and projection in neighborhood commercial districts.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a California ABC license broker to identify, escrow and initiate transfer of an available Type 47 license to 401 Columbus Ave.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Tell the broker the target address is 401 Columbus Ave, SF 94133, census tract 107.02 (over authorized count, so PCN finding required), and that the CUA hearing at Planning will run in parallel. The broker handles the license purchase agreement, escrow, ABC Form 252 (premises-to-premises transfer), posting at the premises, and coordination with ABC's 60-day investigation and public notice period. Budget $100k–$450k for the license purchase and 90–240 days total (catalog ca.abc_type_47). Start this immediately because the CUA cannot be finalized without a license in escrow or available.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with SF Planning whether the restaurant concept is formula retail and obtain the five CUA motions on file at 401 Columbus Ave (Cases 1988.106C, 1997.365C, 2004.0925C, 2007.1256C, 2009.1079C) to review their conditions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email or visit SF Planning's public counter with the business name, ownership structure, and a statement of whether the restaurant shares its name, décor, menu, or standardized features with 11 or more other locations. Also request copies of the five CUA motions on file for 401 Columbus Ave to confirm which conditions remain in effect and whether any are proposed to be changed. Planning needs these answers to complete the CUA application, and formula retail is not permitted in the North Beach NCD so it must be ruled out before filing.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning Department for the Type 47 intensification, including a project description, site photos, floor plan, and a pre-application meeting scheduled within 30 days.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the application is to intensify the existing restaurant use at 401 Columbus Ave by upgrading from the current Type 41 (beer/wine) authorization to a Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place) ABC license, with no physical expansion, no change to the 2,570 sq ft footprint, and no tenant improvements. Describe the restaurant's food-focused operations, menu, seating, and hours (state the closing hour if known, or commit to closing by midnight to avoid a separate hours trigger). Commit to operate as a bona fide eating place per Planning Code §780.3(c)(2)(A) and to provide gross receipts records to Planning on request. Address the undue concentration issue by describing how the restaurant serves a neighborhood need, improves the existing space, and will not create public nuisance (e.g., security plan, waste management, soundproofing if applicable, good-neighbor commitments). Request…

filing_playbook.action: Conduct the mandatory community outreach: post the Planning Department's notice at the site for 30 days and mail notice to all properties within 300 feet at least 20 days before the Commission hearing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Planning will provide the mailing labels and notice template once the CUA is deemed complete. Post the yellow notice in a street-facing window or door where it is visible to the public for the full 30-day period before the hearing. The notice states the proposed Type 47 authorization, the hearing date and time, and how to submit comments or appeals. Proactively meet with the North Beach Neighbors Association, the Telegraph Hill Dwellers, and any registered neighborhood group that Planning identifies, present the concept, and address concerns about noise, trash, hours, and patron behavior before they become hearing testimony. Document these meetings in writing (attendance, concerns raised, your responses) and submit the log to Planning as part of the case file. This outreach is not optional: the December 2022 CUA at 414 Columbus Ave (43 m away) imposed a community liaison condition, and…

filing_playbook.action: Prepare and submit a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) statement to SF Planning and ABC, documenting how the Type 47 license serves the neighborhood despite the tract being over its authorized on-sale license count.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The PCN statement should include: (1) a description of the restaurant's food-focused menu, hours, and bona fide eating place operations; (2) the history of restaurant use at 401 Columbus Ave (36 years, five prior CUAs, existing Type 41); (3) how full bar service is incidental to the dining experience and will not create a bar-like environment; (4) the condition of the space and how the concept improves it (renovation details, if any); (5) neighborhood support letters or petition signatures from nearby residents and businesses; (6) crime and nuisance statistics for the immediate block showing the restaurant will not contribute to existing issues; (7) a security and management plan (staffing, ID checks, cut-off policies, last call protocol, exterior lighting and surveillance). SF Planning will incorporate this into its recommendation to ABC, and ABC will consider it when deciding whether…

filing_playbook.action: Attend the Planning Commission hearing, present the project, respond to Commissioner questions and public comment, and be prepared to accept additional conditions on the spot if the Commission requests them.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Bring the ownership team, architect or designer, and a representative sample of the menu. Present the concept in 5 minutes or less: 'We are upgrading an established restaurant at 401 Columbus Ave from Type 41 to Type 47 to offer a full bar as part of a food-focused dining experience. The space has been a restaurant since 1988 with five prior CUAs. We commit to operating as a bona fide eating place, maintaining the premises and sidewalk, appointing a community liaison, and complying with all standard conditions. We have engaged the neighborhood and addressed their concerns about noise and hours.' If Commissioners ask about hours, state a closing time (e.g., 11 pm or midnight) and commit to it. If they ask about the prior Type 47 history, explain when and why it lapsed (if known) and why reinstating it now serves the neighborhood. If they ask about undue concentration, reference the PCN s…

filing_playbook.action: After the Commission approves the CUA, file the ABC Type 47 transfer application (Form 252) and submit the CUA motion, Planning's recommendation letter, and the PCN materials to ABC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: ABC requires the signed lease, entity formation documents (CA SOS registration), seller's permit, CUA approval motion, and Planning's zoning sign-off letter. Submit these with Form 252 and the transfer fee. ABC will post a 30-day public notice at the premises and send the application to SFPD and Planning for final review. SFPD's ABC Liaison Unit will investigate and may request additional information (e.g., applicant history, criminal background, prior license compliance). Planning will confirm that the CUA covers the Type 47 and that all zoning conditions are met. If no protests are filed and SFPD/Planning recommend approval, ABC issues the license 60–120 days after filing (catalog ca.abc_type_47). If protests are filed or the PCN issue is contested, a hearing before an ABC administrative law judge may be required, adding 2–6 months. Stay in close contact with the ABC investigator and…

filing_playbook.action: Once the CUA is approved and the Type 47 transfer is pending or complete, file for the Health Permit to Operate with SF DPH, including the approved CUA motion and proof of a certified food safety manager on staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online through the DPH Environmental Health portal with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID, federal EIN, menu, equipment list, and a statement that operations are unchanged from the current Cassava restaurant (or describe any changes to food prep or service). DPH will route the application to Planning, which will confirm the CUA approval and zoning compliance. Schedule the pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance and confirm the space meets the 2022–03 plan check approval (if on file) or request a new plan check if the kitchen or service layout has changed. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches approved plans, a certified food safety manager is on staff, and all health code requirements are met. Budget $470 application fee and 14–45 days (catalog sf.health_permit).

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost are for the CUA, the Type 47 license transfer, and the health permit—the three approvals in the entitlement path—and assume they are granted. The CUA takes roughly 120–300 days from filing to Commission decision based on the December 2022 comparable at 414 Columbus Ave (270 days, app:datasf_planning:2022-002108CUA) and typical CUA timelines (catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization equivalent). The Type 47 transfer takes 90–240 days including broker engagement, escrow, ABC posting, investigation, and license issuance (catalog:ca.abc_type_47), and costs $17,000–$450,000 for the license purchase on the open market plus ABC fees; the lower end assumes a distressed or rural-county license, the upper end reflects San Francisco market prices. The health permit takes 14–45 days after CUA approval (catalog:sf.health_permit, $470–$1,000). The CUA filing fee is approximately $3,100 (2026–27 estimate, scaled by construction cost; the concept states no tenant improvements so the base fee applies). Government fees total roughly $20,000–$24,000 (CUA + ABC transfer fee + health permit + business registration + entity formation + other state/local fees from the catalog); the wide cost range is driven entirely by the Type 47 license purchase price, which is a private-market transaction not a government fee. These figures do not include attorney, architect, or broker professional fees, which can add $15,000–$50,000 depending on complexity. The timeline assumes no appeals (a 30-day appeal period follows the CUA decision), no ABC hearing on the PCN issue (which would add 2–6 months), and no significant delays in neighborhood outreach or document preparation. If the formula retail question or the prior CUA condition-amendment question cannot be resolved, or if the Commission denies the CUA, the timeline and cost do not apply.
